architectural_units.name: Security Service
architectural_units.description: Functions as a reverse proxy and load balancer, managing HTTP and HTTPS request routing.

architectural_units.name: Traefik
architectural_units.description: Tool used to implement the Security Service.

architectural_units.name: System Service
architectural_units.description: Serves the web application and interacts with the database and external services.

architectural_units.name: Next.js
architectural_units.description: Framework used to develop the System Service.

architectural_units.name: Data Service
architectural_units.description: Provides the relational database for storing application data.

architectural_units.name: PostgreSQL
architectural_units.description: Database engine used for the Data Service.

architectural_units.name: Prisma
architectural_units.description: ORM used to manage database queries and modifications.

architectural_units.name: React
architectural_units.description: Library used for building user interfaces within the System Service.

architectural_units.name: Authentication Service
architectural_units.description: External service used for user authentication.

architectural_units.name: Google
architectural_units.description: Provider used for the Authentication Service.

architectural_units.name: Cloud Storage Service
architectural_units.description: External service for storing and retrieving files.

architectural_units.name: Amazon S3
architectural_units.description: Product used for the Cloud Storage Service.

architectural_units.name: Payment Processing Service
architectural_units.description: External service for handling payments and subscriptions.

architectural_units.name: Stripe
architectural_units.description: Product used for the Payment Processing Service.

architectural_units.name: Analytics Service
architectural_units.description: External service for tracking and analyzing site traffic.

architectural_units.name: Google Analytics
architectural_units.description: Product used for the Analytics Service.

architectural_units.name: Error Monitoring Service
architectural_units.description: External service for tracking and managing application errors.

architectural_units.name: Sentry
architectural_units.description: Product used for the Error Monitoring Service.

architectural_units.name: Email Service
architectural_units.description: External service for creating, sending, and scheduling emails.

architectural_units.name: Brevo
architectural_units.description: Product used for the Email Service.

architectural_units.name: Docker
architectural_units.description: Platform used to manage the execution of containers for all services.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: Communication protocol managed by Traefik.

architectural_units.name: HTTPS
architectural_units.description: Communication protocol managed by Traefik.
Security Service (Traefik) manages the routing of HTTP and HTTPS requests towards the Next.js application (System Service).
The System Service communicates with the PostgreSQL database (Data Service) using Prisma as ORM.
The System Service interacts with Google for user authentication.
The System Service interacts with Amazon S3 for storing and retrieving files.
The System Service integrates with Stripe to handle payments and subscriptions.
The System Service implements Google Analytics to track and analyze site traffic.
The System Service uses Sentry to track and manage errors in the application.
The System Service connects to Brevo to create, send, and schedule emails.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The architecture of software based on microservices is a design and development approach where an application is built as a collection of small and independent services that communicate with each other.

patterns.name: Component-Based
patterns.description: The Component-Based pattern focuses on building the user interface by creating independent and reusable components.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern
patterns.description: The Observer pattern establishes a one-to-many relationship between objects, where an object known as the subject maintains a list of other objects called observers.

patterns.name: Singleton Pattern
patterns.description: The Singleton pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to that instance.
